summary: R-6 flat cab built 1959 on Klickitat County ground, replacing Simcoe Butte; burned in the 2013 Mile Marker 28 Fire; land described as privately owned, no trespass.

facts.agency: Bureau of Indian Affairs (register); Yakima Indian Agency (Washington Lookouts)

access.note: Willhite: a private timber owner owns the land; access marked landowner-only, no trespass. Register and Firelookout place it on the Yakama Indian Reservation, so ownership is disputed in the sources

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register lists the Bureau of Indian Affairs and places the site on the Yakama Indian Reservation; Firelookout also places it on the reservation; Willhite says a private timber owner owns the land and marks access no-trespass. The story reports both and advises heeding the no-trespass note.
Register says abandoned for several years; Willhite says unused for many years. The story gives both descriptions without choosing one.

notes_for_editor: Built 1959 and the 2013 burn agree across sources. Ownership conflicts (BIA and Yakama Reservation vs a private timber owner per Willhite); the story says so and tells visitors to heed the no-trespass note. Register lists a removal year of 2013 alongside the burn; the story uses the burn, not a separate removal event. No staffing history found. Willhite's 'from the air' remark is the only description of what remains today.
